Repository: encode/httpx
Language: Python

Redundant `boundary` if files/data is empty
If you try to send a post request with empty data and files — you will create a body with one `--boundary--` string, which can break the server.

It's because httpx create MultipartStream for `data={}, files={}`:
https://github.com/encode/httpx/blob/a82adcc933345c6b8cb1623b031eb85723e7665b/httpx/_content_streams.py#L332-L334

And this MultipartStream doesn't have special behavior for empty data/files:
https://github.com/encode/httpx/blob/a82adcc933345c6b8cb1623b031eb85723e7665b/httpx/_content_streams.py#L277-L283

Reproducible example:

```
from httpx.content_streams import encode

stream = encode(data={}, files={}, boundary=b"+++")
print(b"".join([part for part in stream]))
# b'--+++--\r\n'
```

I see two ways to solve it:
1. Check files not only for None but also for emptiness in `_content_streams.decode`
2. Check the count of fields in `MultipartStream.__init__` and doesn't write anything if fields are empty.

I already opened PR (#861) with a test example. If someone tells me which of these options is better, I will be happy to implement it  🙌

import io

import pytest

from httpx import StreamConsumed
from httpx._content_streams import ContentStream, encode


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_base_content():
    stream = ContentStream()
    sync_content = b"".join([part for part in stream])
    async_content = b"".join([part async for part in stream])

    assert stream.can_replay()
    assert stream.get_headers() == {}
    assert sync_content == b""
    assert async_content == b""


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_empty_content():
    stream = encode()
    sync_content = b"".join([part for part in stream])
    async_content = b"".join([part async for part in stream])

    assert stream.can_replay()
    assert stream.get_headers() == {}
    assert sync_content == b""
    assert async_content == b""


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_bytes_content():
    stream = encode(data=b"Hello, world!")
    sync_content = b"".join([part for part in stream])
    async_content = b"".join([part async for part in stream])

    assert stream.can_replay()
    assert stream.get_headers() == {"Content-Length": "13"}
    assert sync_content == b"Hello, world!"
    assert async_content == b"Hello, world!"


@pytest.mark.asyncio
async def test_iterator_content():
    def hello_world():
        yield b"Hello, "
        yield b"world!"

    stream = encode(data=hello_world())
    content = b"".join([part for part in stream])

    assert not stream.can_replay()
    assert stream.get_headers() == {"Transfer-Encoding": "chunked"}
    assert content == b"Hello, world!"

    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError):
        [part async for part in stream]

    with pytest.raises(StreamConsumed):
        [part for part in stream]

item.text:
Fixed the empty-files case in [encode](/testbed/httpx/_content_streams.py:334). When `files={}`, dict data now uses URL encoding, so a POST with `data={}, files={}` has an empty body instead of a multipart closing boundary. Populated files still use multipart encoding.

Added stream and POST request regression tests. All 49 relevant tests pass, and Flake8 passes. The full suite could not run in this sandbox because its network-backed tests require socket creation, which is denied.
